o: The lateral femoral cutaneous nerve is L2, 3
True. The lateral femoral cutaneous nerve comes from the posterior divisions of L2 and L3. (Last's)
The femoral branch of the genitofemoral nerve is L1
The genital branch is L2.
The posterior femoral cutaneous nerve is L5
The infrapatellar branch of the saphenous nerve pierces sartorius near its origin
Above its insertion; the intermediate cutaneous nerve pierces it near its origin.

questions.s: Muscles with dual innervation in the thigh (Last's):
o: Pectineus
Femoral and obturator (or accessory obturator).
Adductor magnus
Obturator and tibial part of sciatic.
Biceps femoris
Long head tibial, short head common peroneal.
Gracilis
Obturator only.
The femoral artery always lies between the saphenous nerve and femoral vein
True. In the adductor canal the femoral artery always lies between the saphenous nerve (lateral, then crossing) and the femoral vein. (Last's)
The femoral vein lies lateral to the artery at the adductor hiatus
Medial at the femoral triangle.
The femoral vein lies medial to the artery at the hiatus
Lateral.
The nerve to vastus medialis runs in the lower part of the canal
In the upper part.
The tibial nerve is the most superficial of the main contents
True. From superficial to deep in the popliteal fossa: tibial nerve, popliteal vein, popliteal artery. (Last's)
The popliteal vein lies between the artery and the nerve
True. The vein is sandwiched between the artery (deepest) and the tibial nerve (most superficial). (Last's)
The common peroneal nerve runs lateral to the biceps tendon
Medial to it, beneath the deep fascia.
The floor from above down is popliteus, capsule, femur
Femur, capsule, popliteus.

questions.s: Structures piercing the roof of the popliteal fossa (Last's):
o: The small saphenous vein
True. The small saphenous vein pierces the roof of the popliteal fossa to join the popliteal vein. (Last's)
The peroneal communicating nerve
True. The peroneal communicating nerve pierces the roof to join the sural nerve. (Last's)
The lateral cutaneous nerve of the calf
True. The lateral cutaneous nerve of the calf pierces the roof over the lateral head of gastrocnemius. (Last's)
The sural nerve
It pierces the deep fascia halfway down the leg.

questions.s: Nerve supply of the knee joint (Last's):
o: The nerve to vastus medialis
Femoral.
The posterior division of the obturator nerve
Accompanying the femoral artery through the hiatus.
Genicular branches of the tibial nerve
True. Genicular branches of the tibial (and common peroneal) parts of the sciatic supply the knee (Hilton's law). (Last's)
The saphenous nerve proper
Not listed; its infrapatellar branch supplies skin.
The femoral nerve comes from posterior divisions of L2, 3, 4
True. The femoral nerve comes from posterior divisions of L2, 3, 4, so it supplies extensors (quadriceps). (Last's)
The obturator nerve comes from anterior divisions of L2, 3, 4
True. The obturator nerve comes from anterior divisions of L2, 3, 4 and supplies the adductors. (Last's)
The accessory obturator is present in about two-thirds
In about one-third.
The accessory obturator nerve supplies adductor longus
It supplies pectineus.
The nerve to quadratus femoris is L4, 5, S1 from anterior divisions
True. The nerve to quadratus femoris (L4, 5, S1, anterior divisions) also supplies inferior gemellus and the hip joint. (Last's)
The inferior gluteal nerve is L5, S1, 2 from posterior divisions
True. The inferior gluteal nerve (L5, S1, 2) comes from posterior divisions and supplies gluteus maximus. (Last's)
The superior gluteal nerve comes from anterior divisions
From posterior divisions (extensor).
The nerve to obturator internus is L4, 5, S1
The ilioinguinal is the collateral branch of the iliohypogastric
True. The ilioinguinal nerve is the collateral branch of the iliohypogastric, running parallel at a lower level. (Last's)
The ilioinguinal supplies the anterior third of the scrotum
And the root of the penis.
The iliohypogastric pierces the external oblique aponeurosis 5 cm above the superficial ring
About 2.5 cm above.
The ilioinguinal enters the inguinal canal through the deep ring
From the side.
C1, C7, C8, L4 and L5 posterior rami give no cutaneous supply
True. The posterior rami of C1, C7, C8, L4 and L5 supply muscles but no skin. (Last's)
Medial branches supply skin in the upper part of the trunk
Lateral branches in the lower part.
T12 is the dividing level between medial and lateral cutaneous branches
About T6.
All lumbar posterior rami supply skin
L4 and L5 do not.
It may arise from the femoral nerve in the iliac fossa
True. The lateral femoral cutaneous nerve may arise from the femoral nerve in the gutter between psoas and iliacus. (Last's)
It lies in a tunnel about 1 cm medial to the ASIS
True. It passes into the thigh in a tunnel in or under the inguinal ligament about 1 cm medial to the ASIS, a site of entrapment (meralgia paraesthetica). (Last's)
Its anterior branch is L2
The anterior branch is L3; the posterior branch L2.
It supplies no peritoneum
It supplies parietal peritoneum of the iliac fossa.
It emerges from the anterior surface of psoas
True. The genitofemoral nerve emerges from the anterior surface of psoas and runs down on it. (Last's)
On the left it is crossed by the inferior mesenteric vein
True. On the left the nerve is crossed by the left colic vessels and inferior mesenteric vein; on the right by the ileocolic artery. (Last's)
On the right it is crossed by the inferior mesenteric vein
By the ileocolic artery.
Its femoral branch supplies cremaster
The genital branch supplies cremaster.
It lies lateral to the femoral sheath
Separated from the artery.
The nerve to vastus medialis is the largest deep branch
True. The nerve to vastus medialis is the largest deep branch and often double; it also supplies the knee. (Last's)
The nerve to pectineus runs in front of the femoral sheath
Behind it.
The saphenous nerve emerges below the anterior border of sartorius
Below the posterior border.
It emerges from the medial border of psoas
Lateral to the lumbosacral trunk.
Its divisions straddle adductor brevis
True. The anterior and posterior divisions of the obturator nerve pass in front of and behind adductor brevis. (Last's)
Its posterior division supplies adductor longus
The anterior division does.
Its anterior division pierces obturator externus
The posterior division does.
The superior gluteal nerve leaves above piriformis
True. The superior gluteal nerve and vessels leave the greater sciatic foramen above piriformis; everything else passes below it. (Last's)
The superior gluteal nerve ends in tensor fasciae latae
True. It runs between gluteus medius and minimus, supplying both, and ends in tensor fasciae latae. (Last's)
The inferior gluteal nerve enters gluteus maximus near its insertion
Near its origin (medial end).
The nerve to quadratus femoris lies superficial to the sciatic nerve
Deep to it, against the ischium.
It remains beneath the deep fascia below gluteus maximus
Unique among cutaneous nerves.
Its perineal branch supplies the lateral posterior scrotum
True. The perineal branch winds round the hamstring origin to the lateral part of the posterior scrotum or labium; the pudendal supplies the medial part. (Last's)
It lies deep to the sciatic nerve
Superficial.
It ends at the popliteal fossa
As far as the lower ends of gastrocnemius.
It is supplied by the artery of the sciatic nerve from the inferior gluteal
The remnant of the axial artery.
It lies a fingerbreadth lateral to the semimembranosus tendon
True. In the thigh the sciatic nerve lies about a fingerbreadth lateral to the semimembranosus tendon, under biceps. (Last's)
The tibial part supplies the short head of biceps
The common peroneal part does.
When it divides high, the tibial part pierces piriformis
The peroneal part pierces piriformis.
It has no muscular branches apart from a few fibres to tibialis anterior
Via the recurrent genicular nerve.
The recurrent genicular nerve supplies the superior tibiofibular joint
True. The recurrent genicular nerve supplies the superior tibiofibular joint, the knee and a few fibres of tibialis anterior. (Last's)
It divides in the substance of peroneus brevis
In peroneus longus.
The lateral cutaneous nerve of the calf supplies the lower half of the peroneal compartment
The upper half.

questions.s: The deep and superficial peroneal nerves (Last's):
o: The deep peroneal nerve supplies the skin of the first cleft
True. The deep peroneal nerve gives cutaneous supply only to the first web space (cleft) between the great and second toes. (Last's)
The superficial peroneal nerve supplies both peronei
Longus and brevis.
The deep peroneal nerve lies medial to the dorsalis pedis artery
Lateral; EHL tendon is medial to the artery.
The superficial peroneal nerve pierces the fascia one-third down the leg
Halfway down.
It passes beneath the fibrous arch of soleus
True. The tibial nerve and posterior tibial vessels pass deep to the fibrous arch of soleus into the deep calf. (Last's)
It divides behind the medial malleolus beneath the flexor retinaculum
True. Behind the medial malleolus, under the flexor retinaculum, the tibial nerve divides into medial and lateral plantar nerves (tarsal tunnel). (Last's)
The sural nerve runs medial to the small saphenous vein at the ankle
Lateral.
The medial calcanean nerve supplies the lateral heel
The weight-bearing skin of the heel.
The medial plantar nerve supplies the first lumbrical
True. The medial plantar nerve supplies abductor hallucis, flexor digitorum brevis, flexor hallucis brevis and the first lumbrical (like the median nerve). (Last's)
The deep branch of the lateral plantar nerve supplies adductor hallucis
True. The deep branch of the lateral plantar nerve supplies adductor hallucis, the lateral three lumbricals and most interossei (like the ulnar). (Last's)
The medial plantar artery lies lateral to the nerve
Medial.
The superficial branch of the lateral plantar nerve supplies the three lateral lumbricals
The deep branch does.

questions.s: Concerning dorsalis pedis and some small nerves (Last's):
o: The anterior tibial becomes dorsalis pedis midway between the malleoli
True. The anterior tibial artery becomes dorsalis pedis in front of the ankle, midway between the malleoli. (Last's)
Dorsalis pedis lies between EHL tendon and the deep peroneal nerve
True. Dorsalis pedis lies between the EHL tendon medially and the deep peroneal nerve laterally, where its pulse is felt. (Last's)
The nerve to quadratus femoris supplies superior gemellus
Inferior gemellus; obturator internus nerve supplies superior gemellus.
The perineal branch of S4 supplies the external anal sphincter
It supplies levator ani parts and coccygeus, and perianal skin.
